title: Workshop on Base Revision of State level Index of Industrial Production during 28–30 October 2026 at Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam
body_text: The three-day Regional Training Workshop on Base Year Revision of the State Level Index of Industrial Production (IIP) commenced at Hotel Dimora International, Thiruvananthapuram, on 28 October 2026. The workshop was organized by Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India, in collaboration with Department of Economics & Statistics (DES), Government of Keralam. The workshop will continue until 30 October 2026. Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), MoSPI, formally inaugurating the workshop. The programme began with lamp lighting by the dignitaries. Inaugural session of the three days workshop was graced by the distinguished dignitaries, including the Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), MoSPI, Shri Gokul G. R., IAS, Special Secretary, Planning & Economic Affairs Department, Government of Keralam, Shri Deepak Dhanawat, Director, MoSPI, Ms. Shailamma K, Director, Directorate of Economics & Statistics, Keralam and by Shri V. K. Sreejan, Additional Director, Directorate of Economics & Statistics, Keralam. The Workshop was attended by approximately 60 participants from 16 States/UTs. Ms. Shailamma K, Director, Directorate of Economics & Statistics, Keralam, welcomed the dignitaries and participants, acknowledged the support of MoSPI and organising the regional training programme, and highlighted the importance of strengthening the technical capacity of State statistical offices for the effective implementation of the IIP base-year revision exercise. Shri Deepak Dhanawat, Director, MoSPI, outlined the objectives and background of the workshop. He has highlighted on the importance of State IIP in tracking the industrial performance if State. He stressed that States should compile the same methodology as the All India IIP. Shri Gokul G. R., IAS, Special Secretary, Planning & Economic Affairs Department, Government of Keralam, presided over the inaugural session. In his presidential address, Shri Gokul G. R., IAS, highlighted the growing public importance of reliable official statistics in a context where economic information is widely discussed through social media and where individual participation in financial and retail investment has increased. He observed that timely, credible and methodologically sound statistics are essential for informed public discussion and evidence-based policy decisions. He stressed that the item basket used for compiling the IIP should reflect the current structure of industry and changes in production patterns. He also emphasised the need to strengthen the quality of primary data collection, minimise measurement errors and ensure that the information furnished by reporting units accurately represents industrial activity. Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), MoSPI, formally inaugurated the workshop. In his inaugural address, Dr. Dalip Singh emphasised the need to align the revised State-level IIP series with the updated national methodology to improve consistency and comparability across States and Union Territories. He referred to 2022–23 as the proposed new base year and underlined the importance of updating the item basket so that the index captures changes in the industrial economy. He also drew attention to the need to improve the availability and quality of data for industrial products and minerals, including major and minor minerals, and to strengthen the systems used for collecting and validating data. The adoption of NIC 2025, appropriate treatment of sectors such as Gas supply, water supply, sewerage and waste management in line with relevant recommendations, and suitable value-based approaches for heterogeneous products were among the methodological considerations highlighted. He encouraged States to strengthen their capacity for regular monthly compilation of the IIP and to ensure that the revised series is robust, timely and comparable. The revision of the base year from 2011–12 to 2022–23 is intended to ensure that the IIP better reflects the present industrial structure, changes in the range of products manufactured and evolving production patterns. The index is an important indicator for monitoring short-term movements in industrial production and supporting economic analysis and policy formulation. The workshop is designed to provide practical and methodological guidance to officers from States and Union Territories on the key stages of the revision exercise, including selection of the item basket and factories, item grouping, preparation of the weighting diagram, data sources and treatment of items classified as Not Elsewhere Classified (NEC). The programme also covers the review of NIC 2025, feedback on the revised National Product Classification (NPC), data-sharing mechanisms, and methodologies for substitution and imputation. Dignitaries on the dais during the inaugural session The first day's technical sessions included a presentation on the new features of the IIP base-year revision by Ms. Ankita Singh, Deputy Director General, MoSPI, followed by presentations on the progress of the revision exercise in States and Union Territories. Sessions also addressed sectors and data sources and the treatment of NEC items. Representatives from 16 States/Union Territories, numbering 60 in total, are participating in the workshop. The sessions scheduled for the following two days will focus on the technical and validation aspects of the revision, with opportunities for States to raise queries and share feedback. The inaugural session concluded with a vote of thanks proposed by Shri V. K. Sreejan, Additional Director, Directorate of Economics & Statistics, Keralam. He expressed gratitude to MoSPI for organising the workshop and providing technical support and acknowledged the cooperation of the Government of Keralam and the participating officers from the States and Union Territories. He also conveyed his appreciation to the dignitaries, resource persons and officials involved in organising the programme.
